results.tests: two sections combined: the 120V duty cycle and the flux-cored polarity
results.ask: I'm running flux-cored on 120V at 100A. How long can I weld before resting, and which socket does my ground clamp go in?
results.text:
**Duty cycle:** At 100 A on 120 V, you get **4 minutes welding, then 6 minutes rest**, repeating every 10-minute period. This is rated 40% duty cycle [p.7, p.19].

**Ground clamp:** For flux-cored (DCEN, gasless), the ground clamp goes in the **Positive (+) socket**, and the Wire Feed Power Cable goes in the Negative (–) socket [p.13]. That's reversed from solid-wire MIG, so double check before you strike an arc.If you push past that 4-minute mark, the machine will thermally shut down and show a warning screen on the LCD until it cools [p.23] — better to back off a bit early than trip it mid-bead.
